findings.title: Ordered creation against counterfeit making
findings.claim: After 31:10's sequence of support, stability, life, water, growth, and pairing, “This is God's creation” names an order that the command to show what others have made tests against. The repeated creation root can carry both the brought-into-being sense and, in the rival verb, a secondary fabrication pressure. The closing wrongdoer and misguidance terms place a failed rival claim in a frame of misplaced agency and direction, with a further darkness metaphor made manifest.
findings.mechanism: The demonstrative points from the focus to the preceding creation display, while خَلْقُ names that display and خَلَقَ turns the same root into the requested rival product. أَرُونِى makes the comparison inspectable. The root branches for wrong placement and path-deviation meet in the verdict; the concrete-act branch bounds wrongdoing to a misassigned creative act, and the available darkness branch adds an image to the explicit manifest error.
findings.reader_payoff: The challenge reads as a test of authorship by visible work. The closing verdict describes disorder in both rightful placement and direction, while the display's operations make the comparison more than a contest between impressive objects.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading, that this is God's created order and that the addressees are asked what others created, stays intact. The concrete-act facet names no crop, timing, or soil example; it is limited here to the rival creative claim. Misplacement and darkness remain secondary root pressures, not literal movement or literal darkness. The pericope comparison does not identify a particular rival artifact.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface supplies the creation, showing, wrongdoer, and manifest-error words; the accepted focus branches supply exact glosses and facets. Trusted channel evidence states that false making substitutes fabrication for an ordered process, and the 31:10 connection supplies the preceding Arabic display. The narrower concrete-act facet is contained explicitly.

findings.title: Purchased discourse as a social substitute
findings.claim: The focus still asks for a rival creation to be shown. Earlier in the pericope, 31:6 describes acquired diversionary speech that occupies attention, turns hearers from God's path, and does so without knowledge. Read beside the focus, this can supply a social mechanism by which counterfeit authorship circulates where an artifact cannot be shown: the answer-shaped substitute may be talk rather than a created product.
findings.mechanism: The HFT before-reading is that the rival creator claim is simply unsupported; its after-reading is that support is manufactured socially, as purchasable talk occupies attention, moves hearers off course, and stands where a created exhibit should stand. The focus's خَلَقَ has a supplied false-production branch and the demand to show a rival result. The attributed 31:6 traces connect purchase, diversion, speech, misguidance, and lack of knowledge to that demand: buying makes the discourse deliberate, diversion occupies attention, report/speech supplies its medium, and deviation returns in the focus diagnosis.
findings.reader_payoff: The question can be heard against a discourse that occupies the place of evidence, so the challenge concerns how an unsupported maker-claim circulates as well as whether a rival artifact exists.
findings.containment: The text does not explicitly equate the purchased speech of 31:6 with a claim that rivals created the world. The HFT source itself preserves the alternative that the speech distracts without directly answering the creation challenge. The 31:6 connection is local thematic context, not proof from creation; the contextual roots and roles remain attributed to a legacy-unbound source.

epistemic.reason: The HFT source is legacy_unbound and its broader packet scope exceeds the declared pericope, though these cited anchors lie within it and the Arabic and stated coordinates agree. The social-substitute link is an explicit inference with a stated distraction-only alternative.

findings.title: From refused hearing to demanded sight
findings.claim: In 31:7, a hearer turns away in pride and behaves as though he did not hear the recited signs; in 31:11, the challenge changes sensory mode and asks to be shown a rival creation. Across the pericope, the latter demand can expose a posture toward receiving evidence, so the earlier scene adds a possible refusal behind what might otherwise look like a neutral lack of evidence.
findings.mechanism: The HFT before-reading treats “show me” as addressed to a neutral observer who lacks evidence; its after-reading allows an observer whose perception has been trained not to yield understanding, so absence of a rival exhibit and refusal of the present exhibit reinforce each other. The attributed trace links turning away, pride, hearing-as-understanding, and weight in the ear to the later imperative to show. The auditory image meets the focus's visual demand: the evidentiary problem may include chosen non-reception, not only the absence of a rival artifact.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear “show me” as a diagnostic challenge to the readiness to take in signs as well as a request for an object.
findings.containment: The HFT source itself preserves the alternative that 31:7 and 31:11 describe different audiences. The earlier text uses a singular hearer and the focus addresses a plural audience, so no identity is asserted; the attributed posture is not generalized to every addressee.

epistemic.reason: The exact 31:7 surface and trace positions support each attributed role, and the focus return is an explicit show imperative. The connection between separate scenes and audiences remains unresolved.

findings.title: Creation as an operating order
findings.claim: The demonstrative in 31:11 can point back to 31:10's ordered creation: support, terrestrial stability, constrained sway, dispersed life, delivered water, growth, and pairing. The focus noun خَلْقُ can also carry the supplied measure/proportion branch, allowing the sequence to read as an operating architecture whose effects form the exhibit rivals are asked to match.
findings.mechanism: The HFT before-reading treats creation as a collection of impressive made objects; its after-reading treats it as an operating architecture of support, damping, distribution, transfer, emergence, and pairing that rivals must match. The exact 31:10 traces place stabilizing supports beside the motion they constrain, water beside the growth it enables, and growth beside paired variety. Those distinct operations meet the focus demonstrative and its measured-creation branch. The sequence therefore supports an integrated reading, while the causal coupling and coordinated-control formulation remain an inference from their order and stated roles.
findings.reader_payoff: The creation challenge can be measured against operations and consequences, not only against a collection of impressive objects.
findings.containment: 31:10 can still be read as a catalogue of divine works united by attribution. The system-like integration is an inference from the stated order and the explicit support, stability, water, and growth relations; it does not assert that every listed operation is one tightly coupled mechanism.

epistemic.reason: The 31:10 Arabic and trace coordinates are supplied and the focus B001 branch has an exact registry gloss and facet. The HFT reader identity is legacy_unbound, and its coordinated-control reading is explicitly an inference with a catalogue alternative.

findings.title: Visible effects and the support not shown
findings.claim: The 31:10 description places a visual register beside supports explicitly negated; 31:11 then asks to be shown what rival agents have created. The command can require an accountable, inspectable display without requiring the supporting relation itself to appear as a visible column: effects can be shown even where the support is not presented as an object.
findings.mechanism: The focus imperative belongs to the supplied show-someone branch. The HFT trace connects the preceding sight occurrence to that imperative and places the negated support occurrence beside it. This contact changes “show me requires a directly visible manufactured object” into a distinction between an inspectable effect and a supporting relation that may not itself be seen.
findings.reader_payoff: The demand remains concrete and answerable while leaving room for an effect to be visible even if its support is not itself displayed.
findings.containment: The attachment of تَرَوْنَهَا in 31:10 may be to the heavens or to the supports. If it describes the heavens, the invisible-support contrast is weaker, though the sequence still places sight before the focus's show imperative. This does not claim that every cause is invisible or that the focus abandons its demand for an inspectable product.

epistemic.reason: The exact 31:10 and 31:11 Arabic and stated HFT coordinates support the visual/support contact, but the target morphology and pronoun attachment are not supplied independently. The trace is retained as attributed contextual evidence with both attachments visible.
